artifacts.summary: Resolves the absorb/depend/expand question for tasks 635/636/628 (recommends depend-on, not absorb/expand), confirms F5 (prompt-time injection scoping) is already a closed, vendor-owned residual with no further local action, and narrows the open F6 capture-stall question with live-machine evidence pointing to a manual-invocation gap rather than a code defect, recommending it be appended to task 636 rather than filed separately.

memory_candidates.content: Sapience's live per-turn transcript capture (sapience_cli.py's cc_capture/cc_flush, posting to POST /v1/cc/turn via a ~/.sapience/cc-outbox/ queue, gated on a server-driven cc_sessions flag in cli-state.json) is architecturally SEPARATE from the batch extraction pipeline that populates ~/.sapience/extracted.json and pending_kos.jsonl. The two can diverge independently: cc-outbox/ may never have fired (directory absent) while the batch pipeline ran once and then stalled, with no systemd timer or crontab entry driving either on this machine -- the batch pipeline's triggering verb (sapience sync/review/coverage) appears to be manual-only.

verify-sapience-context-scoping.sh's RESIDUAL_HOLDS outcome is documented, in the script's own header and in injection-site-scoping.md, as the EXPECTED green state today (a vendor-owned foreclosure with no local remedy), not a failure condition. A task description that frames eliminating RESIDUAL_HOLDS as an acceptance criterion is describing something this repository has no mechanism to close -- check the extension's own domain docs before writing an acceptance bar against one of its documented verification probes.
